messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw a ~6% drop in prefix cache hit rate after last kernel/serializer deploy. graphs show it lines up with a bunch of tool-call heavy requests.
trent: can you paste a repro or a couple of failing examples? :thinking_face:
maya: pasting two representative payload snippets. most misses share one pattern: tool_call args serialized as an array vs object. example (miss):

maya: ```
{
  "tool": "search",
  "args": [{"q": "foo"}, {"filters": {}}]
}
```

maya: and older hit entries looked like (hit):

maya: ```
{
  "tool": "search",
  "args": {"q": "foo", "filters": {}}
}
```

olivia: that would definitely change the serialized bytes. our current keyer just does a raw bytes hash of the prompt+toolpayload blob, so ordering wins/loses here. :grimacing:
trent: two parts to fix: JSON args canonicalization (stable deterministic ordering) and make sure tokenizer/version is part of the signature. do we currently include tokenizer.version or only a token-hash?
maya: we add tokenizer.hash for some models but not a human-readable version string — the hash fluctuates across small rebuilds and causes churn in keys.
profiling-bot: perf-profile: cohort diffs -> serialization_cpu +18% in prefix path, kernel_batch_size +2, kv_lookup p95 flat.
sre-bot: FYI deploy 2026-03-16T17:04 rolled serializer v2->v3; rollout-monitor flagged hitrate dip and created incident stub.
olivia: proposed key schema: concat(namespace, model, model_rev, tokenizer_version, normalize(prompt), stable-toolargs_crp) where namespace = system_prompt_hash to isolate system changes.
trent: normalize(prompt) needs to be careful: keep assistant/system instruction semantics (newlines and leading whitespace sometimes matter), but trim trailing spaces, collapse duplicate medium whitespace, and normalize control characters.
maya: also: when system prompt changes we should not silently invalidate the whole cache across customers; namespace separation keeps old keys valid and prevents accidental mass misses.
olivia: rollout plan (sketch):
1) implement JSON args canonicalizer (sort keys, collapse arrays of singletons where appropriate) behind ff.
2) include tokenizer_version string in signature (behind same ff).
3) run 10% cohort for 48h, collect hit/miss + correctness eval on sample prompts.
4) if stable, expand 25% -> 50% -> 100% with TTL warmup of previous keys for 24h between each jump.
trent: test matrix: permutations of arg ordering, missing optional args, functions with named vs positional arg variants, system prompt minor edits. add unit tests and a small perf harness to assert cpu regression <5%.
maya: for an immediate mitigation: patch prefix matcher to try a semantically-normalized fallback on miss (i.e., attempt canonicalize-toolargs and re-check hit) so we can avoid full rollout pressure. cost: extra CPU on misses but should be small.
profiling-bot: cohort-run summary: 10k reqs, baseline hitrate 0.71, after toolargs-normalizer hitrate -> 0.83 for tool-heavy cohort, cpu +3% overall.
olivia: nice. want to expand to 25% tomorrow morning in low-traffic window. @oncall can you coordinate?
trent: I'll draft a tiny RFC with the key layout, tests, and rollout steps and link to the perf dashboard.
maya: quick local repro command for devs:

maya: ```bash
python tools/repro_prefetch.py --model meta/llama-2-7b --cases=toolargs-ordering --profile
```

olivia: note: adding tokenizer_version reduces surprise during tokenizer rebuilds but will increase churn at explicit upgrades — decide policy to only flip for stable tokenizer releases.
trent: agreed. also add a metric for key-churn after any tokenizer deploy.
maya: thanks team — filing follow-ups in eng-runtime and will post the dashboard link once cohort metrics are in. :thumbsup:
